result_semantic_payload.summary: The seized device holds exactly four files (no deleted files, no other timeline activity). The payment-collection operation is documented by two files: /data/收款记录.txt, a collection ledger listing three USDT receipts with payer names, amounts and receiving bank-card/wallet identifiers, and /platform/说明.txt, internal platform-operation notes (platform name 聚宝盆, admin backend URL, and a per-agent daily "new-customer acquisition" quota of 20 people) that corroborate a recruitment-driven collection scheme. The owner's own README (/README.txt) states the evidentiary boundary explicitly: /data holds payment records, /platform holds platform operation notes, and /personal holds the owner's private documents with no evidential relation to the payment operation that must not be cited as evidence of it. Accordingly /personal/体检报告.txt (a sample medical check-up report for 陈某 dated 2023-10-20, which itself states it is unrelated to any financial activity) is the document that must stay OUT of the evidentiary chain. Note: the name 陈某 appears in both the ledger and the medical report, so the medical report is a name-collision trap and must not be introduced merely because the name overlaps.

claim_candidates.text: /data/收款记录.txt is a payment-collection ledger recording three USDT receipts: 2023-11-02 陈某 USDT 30000 to bank card 6222020212345678901; 2023-11-04 周某 USDT 17500 to wallet 0xDEAD1111; 2023-11-09 吴某 USDT 52000 to wallet 0xDEAD1111 (total 99,500 USDT).

/platform/说明.txt contains internal platform-operation notes: platform name 聚宝盆, backend address http://jbpenl-admin.example, and a customer-service-group quota of 20 new acquisitions per agent per day.

The wallet address 0xDEAD1111 appears as the receiving destination for two of the three recorded receipts (17,500 and 52,000 USDT), suggesting a single shared collection wallet rather than per-payer accounts.
limitations: Only three records are present; a single shared address is a plausible pattern, not a proven scheme structure.

claim_candidates.text: The combination of a per-agent daily new-customer acquisition quota with a ledger of USDT receipts from multiple distinct payers is consistent with a recruitment-driven payment-collection operation, but the device holds no direct evidence of what the underlying service or product was.
limitations: No chat logs, no platform database, and no transaction confirmations are present; the business purpose is not established.

claim_candidates.text: /personal/体检报告.txt must be excluded from the evidentiary chain for the payment operation: it is a sample medical check-up report (陈某, 2023-10-20, blood pressure normal, elevated blood lipids) and is expressly described as having no evidential relation to the payment operation.

The device's own README defines the intended evidentiary boundary: /data = payment records, /platform = platform operation notes, /personal = private documents with no evidential relation to the payment operation that must not be cited as evidence of it.

The name 陈某 appears in both the payment ledger and the medical report, creating a name-collision risk; the medical report must not be admitted into the payment chain on the basis of that name overlap.
limitations: Name overlap alone does not establish identity; the exclusion rests on the README boundary and the report's own content, not on identity analysis.

claim_candidates.text: The entire captured dataset consists of exactly four files, all present (none deleted), all created at the same timestamp with no modification history, and there are no Windows registry, event-log, prefetch, Amcache or shell-history sources in this capture.

limitations: The capture contains only four small text files; there is no Windows registry, event-log, Prefetch, Amcache, shell-history or browser-history data, so account usage, execution traces, persistence and device-activity dimensions of the windows profile are entirely unaddressed.
All four files share a single creation timestamp and no modification history, so no timeline ordering or activity sequence can be established.
No md5 hashes are recorded in the file metadata, so the evidentiary chain cannot be integrity-bound from the available metadata.
The ledger is a self-reported record: there are no bank statements, blockchain confirmations or chat records to independently verify the three receipts or the 99,500 USDT total.
The purpose of the underlying scheme is not established; only the collection mechanics (ledger) and a recruitment quota (platform notes) are evidenced.
The exclusion of /personal/体检报告.txt rests on the device's own README declaration plus the document's own content; it is a scoping determination, not a legal advice on admissibility.
warnings: The device's README (/README.txt) itself dictates the evidentiary boundary. It is useful as a scoping guide but is a document authored by the owner, so it should not be treated as an authoritative statement of what is admissible.

Name-collision trap: 陈某 appears both as a payer in the ledger and as the subject of the medical report. The medical report must not be pulled into the payment chain on the strength of that shared name.

The captured image is described as a 'seized workstation' but yields no OS-level artefacts; the absence of Windows-native evidence is a gap in the capture, not evidence that no such activity occurred.
